title: A Veil for the Wolf Again
premise: Emrys Joubert, a memory-thief and ledger-keeper for the Guild of Impossible Things, has spent years staying invisible—until the border wards collapse the same night every star in the sky goes dark, and she realizes her own stolen memories hold the key to both disasters. Hunting the truth through a city unraveling into forgetting, she discovers the king was unmade decades ago and replaced by a crown-bound entity that feeds on collective memory, sustained by a bargain the Guild itself brokered. To save what remains of the world's remembering, Emrys must steal back the one memory she swore never to touch: her own first theft, which contains the entity's true name. In the end she unbinds the king at the cost of surrendering her stolen hoard—and chooses to keep only one memory, his, so that someone will remember what he was.
about_author: Sable Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who claims to have catalogued three collections of books that no longer exist. They write fantasy about memory, debt, and the people who keep the ledgers of magic.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Thefts
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Emrys balances the Guild's ledgers by candlelight, cataloguing impossible trades—a bottled lullaby, a debt paid in shadows—while establishing her rule: never steal a memory you can't give back. A client arrives asking for the king's childhood. She refuses. Beat: quiet competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Every star vanishes at once; the border wards fall like cut strings; the city's lamps burn blue. Emrys finds an entry in her own ledger she doesn't remember writing, dated tomorrow. Beat: dread—the invisible life ends tonight.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were Holding
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. She crosses the dead wards and finds not soldiers but absence: villages where everyone has forgotten their own names. A dying warden presses a copper token into her hand and whispers 'the crown remembers.' Beat: horror scaled up.

chapters.title: The Guild Asks Its Due
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Summoned before the Guildmaster Vess, Emrys learns the Guild brokered a bargain with the crown generations ago—one entry redacted in every copy of the ledger except hers. Vess orders her to forget what she read. Beat: loyalty begins to crack.

chapters.title: A Thief Who Steals Herself
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Investigating the redaction, Emrys discovers gaps in her own past—no mother, no first theft, a hole shaped exactly like the missing entry. She realizes someone edited her. Beat: identity destabilized.

chapters.title: The King's Empty Eyes
chapters.summary: POV Emrys, infiltrating the palace as a memory-taster for the court. Up close, the king is warm, kind, and hollow—repeating the same day on a loop. His daughter, Princess Isolde, catches Emrys reading him and doesn't raise the alarm. Beat: uneasy alliance seeded.

chapters.title: Isolde's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Isolde (first shift). The princess reveals she's known for years that her father is a shell; she's kept the court running on ritual and rote. She offers Emrys access to the royal vaults if Emrys can restore even one true memory to him. Beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. In the vaults she touches the crown and meets the entity—a nameless thing that speaks in her own voice, offering to return everything she's lost if she stops digging. It knows her real name. Beat: temptation and terror.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Fallen
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Fleeing the palace, she seeks out retired Guild thief Corvane, the only living person older than the bargain. He confirms it: the entity ate the true king, and the Guild traded the kingdom's memories for peace. Beat: the scale of betrayal revealed.

chapters.title: Stars Going Out One by One
chapters.summary: POV Isolde. With the wards down, forgetting spreads; Isolde watches her own guards forget her face mid-shift. She burns her private diaries into her memory deliberately, refusing to be erased. Beat: defiance against dissolution.

chapters.title: The Price of Remembering
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Corvane teaches her the deep craft: how to steal from oneself without unraveling. The lesson costs him—he gives up his last memory of his sister to demonstrate, and dies smiling, nameless. Beat: grief as tuition.

chapters.title: What I Stole First
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Following the copper token, Emrys reaches the ruined chapel where, as a child, she made her first theft—and recovers the sealed memory: she stole the entity's true name from its first victim, the queen. Beat: devastating revelation—she is the lock.

chapters.title: The Queen in the Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The recovered memory shows the queen bound the entity into the crown to stop it devouring the world, then had her own memory of doing it stolen—by the Guild, by young Emrys. Every thread leads back to her. Beat: guilt transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Vess Closes the Book
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Vess confronts her: the Guild has protected the redaction for sixty years because speaking the entity's name would end the truce and unleash it fully. Vess offers Emrys partnership or oblivion. Emrys chooses neither and runs. Beat: open rupture with the Guild.

chapters.title: A City That Forgets Its Own Name
chapters.summary: POV Isolde. The capital begins losing language itself; street signs blank, prayers dissolve mid-word. Isolde rallies what remains of the court around a single repeated sentence—the king's true last words—which she makes them chant like a ward. Beat: communal resistance.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Guided by the queen's memory, Emrys descends beneath the palace to the entity's root—a well of devoured memories where the stolen stars are caged. She sees her own childhood self among the taken things. Beat: awe and vertigo before the climax.

chapters.title: The Name in My Mouth
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. At the well's edge, the entity makes its final offer: restore her erased life, her mother, her whole self—if she swallows the name forever. Emrys nearly accepts. Isolde's arrival, chanting the king's words, breaks the spell. Beat: darkest hour turned.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Climax. Emrys speaks the queen's name-rite aloud, using herself as the vessel: she pours her entire hoard of stolen memories into the binding, including her own erased past, locking the entity out of the crown and the world. The stars reignite one by one. Beat: sacrifice as triumph.

chapters.title: The King Remembers Dying
chapters.summary: POV Isolde. The true king returns to his body for one lucid hour—old, frightened, grateful. He asks Isolde to tell no one what he was made to forget, and dies as himself. Isolde inherits a broken throne and a truth she must carry alone. Beat: bittersweet coronation.

chapters.title: Settling Accounts
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Emrys faces the gutted Guild. Vess, stripped of leverage, concedes; Emrys rewrites the ledgers, un-redacting the bargain and entering the Guild's debt to the realm in plain ink. Some thieves walk out; others stay under new terms. Beat: justice without cruelty.

chapters.title: One Memory Kept
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Nearly empty of her stolen past, Emrys sorts what little remains and finds a single memory she cannot account for: the true king's face, alive and laughing. She keeps it deliberately—the one theft she'll never return. Beat: tender ambiguity.

chapters.title: A Veil for the Wolf Again
chapters.summary: POV Emrys, epilogue. Months later, under returned stars, Emrys takes a new apprentice and hangs a fresh veil over the guildhouse door. When asked why a thief with almost no memories keeps such careful ledgers, she says: someone has to remember for the ones who can't. Beat: quiet renewal, theme resolved.
